prompt:
Create pixel-art pieces for a modern 16-bit-style top-down RPG town map (three-quarter overhead view, like a classic SNES JRPG town).

Image 1 is a PLACEMENT GUIDE on a magenta page: fill each grey box edge to edge with the piece described for it. Do not copy the grey colour.

Image 2 is the HOUSE STYLE: the approved walking sprite of a character from this game at the same pixel scale as the map (about 90 sprite pixels tall). Match its sprite-pixel size, its outlines and its flat 2-3 tone shading with light from the upper left.

Image 3 is approved art from this same game map: match its colours, outline weight and shading exactly.
Image 4 is approved art from this same game map: match its colours, outline weight and shading exactly.

Pieces:
- the top-left box (96x96 sprite pixels): a SEAMLESS texture (left edge continues into the right edge, top into bottom). the top of a thick grey stone town wall seen from above: the walkway along the top of the wall, paved with large flat light-grey stone slabs with thin dark joints, evenly spread, no battlements, no edges.
- the top-right box (96x96 sprite pixels): a SEAMLESS texture (left edge continues into the right edge, top into bottom). mossy grey stone blocks of a river embankment seen from above: small squared stones with dark joints and a little green moss in some joints, evenly spread.
- the middle-left box (96x48 sprite pixels): a strip that repeats SEAMLESSLY left to right (its top and bottom edges are real edges). the outer front face of the same grey stone town wall seen from the front: courses of large grey stone blocks with dark mortar, a slightly lighter coping course along the top edge and a darker, shadowed base course along the bottom edge; no openings.
- the middle-centre box (48x48 sprite pixels): a single complete piece filling the box. the same wall face (same stone courses, coping and base) with a dark semicircular stone arch opening at the bottom centre, about half the box wide, where blue river water flows out under the wall.
- the middle-right box (48x48 sprite pixels): a single complete piece filling the box. the same wall face (same stone courses, coping and base) with one narrow dark vertical arrow slit in the centre.
- the bottom-left box (96x48 sprite pixels): a strip that repeats SEAMLESSLY left to right (its top and bottom edges are real edges). the deck of a small stone footbridge seen from above, for walking left to right: pale stone paving running across, with a low stone parapet along the top edge and another along the bottom edge.

Draw each piece as one continuous picture with no lines dividing it into squares. Render as true pixel art: every sprite pixel a hard-edged square, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no blur. Between the boxes: solid flat magenta (#FF00FF), no text.
